risks: The guard is structural, but it measures syntax: a provider could satisfy it by calling ensure_tenant_access and ignoring the exception. That is acceptable here because ensure_tenant_access ENFORCES by raising, and ignoring a raise requires an explicit bare except -- which the test cannot see and review must. Do not mistake the guard for a runtime proof; tests/authentication/test_tenant_access_demo.py remains the behavioural evidence.
A bare import of the seam is not enforcement. The first detector accepted one. Any future relaxation of _calls_seam back to name-matching silently reopens the hole the demo provider fell through.

decisions_this_run: Derive the provider set from the source tree instead of listing it. A hardcoded list is the same defect as the docstring enumeration, one refactor later.

Treat delegation to an enforcing collaborator as satisfaction, but verify it against the real class body in this tree. This is what keeps the session-cookie path honest: moving the check out of ResolveSession.run breaks the test instead of vacating it.

Require an actual call, not a reference. The probe proved a mention passes and enforces nothing; resolve_tenant_access additionally requires the DENIED comparison, so a discarded result cannot satisfy the test.
Record non-provider modules with a reason each, plus a test that fails when an exclusion goes stale. Skipping unknown files would let the next module hide.

Do not fold this guard into test_layering.py. That file enforces import-boundary rules between layers; this one enforces a call-graph invariant inside infrastructure/identity. Different failure messages, different fix guidance.
